values.title: Fix it, don't replace it
values.body: We design for repair first. A pan that can be re-seasoned beats one that can't be scratched.
values.example: In 2025 we re-seasoned 3,100 customer pans for free instead of selling replacements.

values.title: Cook with it first
values.body: Nothing ships until the team has cooked with it for a month, outdoors and at home.
values.example: The Cable Fold grate went through eleven prototypes and two camping trips.

values.title: Answer like a neighbour
values.body: Customer care replies within a day, in plain words, from someone who's used the pan.

values.title: Waste less than we did last year
values.body: Every year we cut scrap iron, packaging and shipping miles — and publish the numbers.
values.example: Our 2025 scrap rate was 2.1%, down from 4.8%.

value.title: Foundry Technician (Finishing)
value.summary: Turn rough castings into pans people keep for fifty years. You'll own grinding, machining and the first seasoning coat, and within a year you'll train the next technician.
value.about: Every Caldera pan passes through finishing: grinding the cooking surface smooth, machining the base flat and baking on the first coat of seasoning. It's skilled, physical work in a small team that cares about every pan.
responsibilities: Grind and polish cooking surfaces to a 0.2 mm tolerance
Run the CNC lathe for base flattening
Apply and bake the first seasoning coat
Inspect every pan and log defects
Keep the finishing bay safe and clean
requirements: Two years in a machine shop, foundry or fabrication
Able to work 7am–3:30pm, Monday to Friday
bonusPoints: You cook with cast iron at home

value.heading: One skillet, a borrowed foundry and a lot of burnt eggs
value.mission: We make cookware for people who cook outside, built to be repaired, re-seasoned and handed down.
value.story:
Caldera started in 2017 with one skillet, cast on weekends in a borrowed foundry in Bend. Ana and Luis wanted a pan light enough to carry to camp and tough enough to sit in coals.

We burned four hundred eggs getting the cooking surface right.

Ana Vidal, co-founder

Nine years later we cast every piece in our own foundry, two miles from where the first one was poured.

milestones.title: The first skillet
milestones.body: Poured on a Saturday in a borrowed foundry. It cracked. The second one didn't.
